title: Latency-first cost optimizer with staged rollback and anomaly containment
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: We need an automated optimizer that recommends and applies batching/caching config changes to reduce per-token cost, but during apply it must guarantee customer latency and throughput SLOs. Prior experiments showed both large cost wins and transient latency spikes when aggressive microwindowing or KV-caching heuristics were applied without containment. Goal: implement a Latency-First Cost Optimizer (LFCO) that (1) generates per-route batching and cache recommendations, (2) applies changes in staged, canaried steps with runtime limiters, and (3) contains and rolls back changes automatically on SLO regressions or anomaly signals. Success metrics: median tail latency change <= +5% for P50/P95/P99, throughput maintained within +/-5% of baseline, cost per 1M tokens reduced by >= 12% on average for routes opted in, false rollback rate < 3% over first 30 days.
design_summary: LFCO comprises three components: a Recommendation Engine, a Safe-Apply Orchestrator, and a Guardrail Monitor. The Recommendation Engine consumes route telemetry (latency distributions, seq-length histograms, KV cache hit rates, model variant mappings) and suggests: batch_size targets, micro-window timings, prefix-KV cache expiration and warmup hints, and quantization/variant fallbacks. Recommendations are scored by estimated cost delta and predicted SLO impact. The Safe-Apply Orchestrator executes staged application of config deltas: shadow-preview -> 0.5% traffic -> 2% -> 10% -> full. Each stage is controlled by a runtime limiter that enforces absolute latency ceilings per route and per-model. The Guardrail Monitor uses multi-signal anomaly detection (EWMA drift on P95, dynamic z-score on error rate, queue-depth slope) to trigger automatic pause/rollback and to mark recommendations as unsafe. When triggered, the system performs a fast rollback (configuration patch revert) and a quarantine step where the recommendation is blacklisted for the route for a configurable cooldown period. The design includes a dry-run mode for customers and an opt-in toggle per workspace.
non_goals: Not building new model quantization pipelines in this ticket. Not addressing autoscaling capacity expansion (separate infra work). Not enabling recommendations for private on-prem deployments until runtime-1.23 compatibility tests pass.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal shadow run against 5 high-volume sandbox routes for 2 weeks. 2) Opt-in beta for 10 enterprise customers (engineering-led) with manual approvals. 3) Auto-apply for low-risk routes (static short seq-length, historically stable P95) with 30-day guardrail holds. 4) Global opt-in gated by a monitored threshold: if >3 auto-rollbacks per 100 routes in 7d, revert auto-apply and investigate.
observability_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-route cost delta, P50/P95/P99 trend, applied-config timeline, rollback events, recommendation health. Alerts: latency SLO breach (P95 over threshold for 5m), burst error spike (5xx > baseline + 3x), rollback storm (>5 rollbacks in 15m). Anomaly reasons are recorded in event logs for postmortem. Add a feature flag to annotate traces with optimizer-phase metadata for tracing and flamegraphs.
failure_modes_and_mitigation: 1) False positives from noisy metrics -> use minimum-stage dwell time and require multi-signal agreement before rollback. 2) Rolling regressions across dependent routes -> implement topological apply ordering and cross-route dependency checks. 3) State drift in KV caches after rollback -> include cold-warm remake plan (prefetch expired prefixes) and gradual traffic ramp-down.
metrics_to_track: P50_latency_ms_before, P50_latency_ms_after, P95_latency_ms_before, P95_latency_ms_after, P99_latency_ms_before, P99_latency_ms_after, throughput_rps, cost_per_1M_tokens_usd, cache_hit_rate, applied_recommendation_count, rollback_count, false_rollback_rate, time_to_rollback_seconds.
safety_limits_config: Configurable at workspace and global level. Examples: route_latency_ceiling_ms (absolute), max_batch_multiplier (<=2x baseline), kv_cache_ttl_min_ms (>=1000ms), min_stage_duration_seconds (>=300), rollback_cooldown_hours (>=1). Default safe profile applied to all auto-applies.
integration_points: Telemetry: via existing observability pipeline (metrics + traces). Runtime: config REST endpoints and /v2/routing control plane. Console: new 'Optimizer' panel under Console -> Performance for approvals and history. SDK: SDK exposes opt-in flags and dry-run toggles. PRs: GitHub PR link will be added under comments when ready.
privacy_and_security_considerations: Recommendations operate on aggregated telemetry; no raw customer prompt content is used. Workspace-specific configs are encrypted at rest and access-controlled. For Private deployments, require additional compatibility and KMS approvals before enabling auto-apply.
next_steps: 1) Finalize Recommendation Engine scoring weights (action: Ethan). 2) Implement runtime limiter hooks and an emergency rollback API (action: infra team). 3) Build Guardrail Monitor prototype and run against sandbox routes (action: Aisha + QA). 4) Draft beta onboarding and console UX flows for approvals (action: PM).
